## Universal cq reformulation

The universal target is equivalent to the following assertion for every cq state XBE:

    I(B:E) - I(B:E|X) <= I_acc(X:BE).

Necessity: take A=BE and identity channel. Sufficiency: apply this assertion to the output, then use chi(X:BE)<=chi(X:A) and I_acc(X:BE)<=I_acc(X:A). The entropy identity is exact.

## Pure-input equivalence to a squashed-entanglement inequality

For pure ensemble {p_x, |psi_x>_A}, introduce

    |Omega>_{RR'A} = sum_x sqrt(p_x) |x>_R |x>_{R'} |psi_x>_A,
    omega_RR' = Tr_A |Omega><Omega|.

This is a maximally correlated state. Write H=H(p), and use logarithms consistently (bits below). Known identities give

    E_F(omega) = H - I_acc(X:A),
    E_D(omega) = H - S(omega) = H - chi(X:A).

For any isometry V:A->BE, let |phi_x>=V|psi_x>. Its induced extension omega_RR'B has

    S(RB)=S(R'B)=H + sum_x p_x S(phi_x^B),
    S(RR'B)=S(E),
    S(B)=S(B).

Consequently

    I(R:R'|B) = 2H - chi(X:B)-chi(X:E).

Every extension of omega is obtained by a channel on the purifier A, and every such channel admits an isometry A->BE. Therefore the pure-input target for all ensembles/channels is EXACTLY equivalent to

    E_F(omega) + E_D(omega) <= 2 E_sq(omega)

for every maximally correlated omega.

Allowing an arbitrary rather than isometric broadcast channel causes no problem in the pure-input reduction: dilate A->BEF and put F with either receiver; dropping F can only decrease the corresponding Holevo information.

This does NOT establish the mixed-input target. Purifying the input states changes both chi and I_acc, so the pure-input statement cannot simply be applied to the original mixed ensemble.

## Classical extensions do satisfy the entanglement inequality

For a classical extension sum_y q_y omega_y \otimes |y><y|, every omega_y remains supported on the maximally correlated subspace. For each omega_y,

    I(R:R')_{omega_y} = H(diag omega_y) + E_D(omega_y),
    E_F(omega_y) <= H(diag omega_y).

Both E_F and E_D on maximally correlated states are convex (the latter is relative entropy of coherence under the canonical identification). Thus

    sum_y q_y I(R:R')_{omega_y} >= E_F(omega)+E_D(omega).

## A complete operator formulation for the equiprobable binary pure case

For density matrices r,s define

- c(r,s) = Tr(sqrt(r) sqrt(s)), the unsquared affinity;
- J(r,s) = S((r+s)/2) - (S(r)+S(s))/2;
- e(c) = h2((1+sqrt(1-c^2))/2);
- f(c) = h2((1+c)/2) + 1 - e(c).

The target for every equiprobable two-element pure ensemble and every isometric broadcast channel is equivalent to the operator inequality

    2 J(r,s) <= f(c(r,s))

for density matrices of arbitrary finite dimension.

### Necessity

Use pure output states vec(sqrt(r)) and vec(sqrt(s)). They are normalized and have inner product c. Their B marginals are r,s, and their E marginals are their transposes. Thus their marginal Holevo sum is 2J. The input Holevo information is h2((1+c)/2), and its accessible information is 1-e(c).

### Sufficiency (symmetrization)

Represent arbitrary normalized pure outputs as vec(M_0), vec(M_1), with rectangular matrices M_i. Pad if needed. Their overlap is c=|Tr(M_0 M_1^dagger)|. Define positive matrices

    R_i = [sqrt(M_i M_i^dagger) direct-sum sqrt(M_i^dagger M_i)] / sqrt(2).

Their Hilbert-Schmidt norms equal one. The density matrices r_i=R_i^2 have Holevo quantity

    J(r_0,r_1) = [chi(X:B)+chi(X:E)]/2.

This follows directly from the equal-weight block entropy identity. Moreover

    c' = Tr(R_0 R_1) >= |Tr(M_0 M_1^dagger)| = c.

For completeness, writing M_i=U_i D_i V_i, Hilbert-Schmidt Cauchy–Schwarz gives

    |Tr(M_0 M_1^dagger)|^2
    <= Tr(sqrt(M_0 M_0^dagger) sqrt(M_1 M_1^dagger))
       * Tr(sqrt(M_0^dagger M_0) sqrt(M_1^dagger M_1)),

and arithmetic–geometric mean gives the claim. Both summands of f(c) decrease on [0,1]. Hence the operator inequality implies

    chi(X:B)+chi(X:E) = 2J(r_0,r_1) <= f(c') <= f(c).

The symmetrization technique also appears in Ahmed–Smith, arXiv:2609.14031v1 (2026), https://arxiv.org/html/2609.14031v1 . Their nonattainment theorem does not resolve the inequality above.

## Stronger spectral bridge candidate

Write r=sum_i lambda_i |i><i| and s=sum_j mu_j |j><j|. Define classical distributions

    P_ij=lambda_i |<i|j>|^2,
    Q_ij=mu_j |<i|j>|^2.

Candidate, not yet proved universally:

    2 J(r,s) <= h2((1+c)/2) + JS(P,Q).

# Spectral entropy bridge: exact partial results

Let J=JS(r,s), N=JS(P,Q), c=Tr(sqrt(r)sqrt(s)), and H(x)=h_2((1+x)/2). The candidate is 2J-N <= H(c).

## Exact canonical-purification reformulation

Put |a>=|sqrt(r)>, |b>=|sqrt(s)> and Omega_AB=(|a><a|+|b><b|)/2. Then both marginals are m=(r+s)/2 up to transpose, S(Omega)=H(c), and

    I(A:B)_Omega - [S(r)+S(s)] = 2J-H(c).

Measuring A in an r eigenbasis and B in the conjugate s eigenbasis gives conditional distributions P_ij=lambda_i |U_ij|^2 and Q_ij=mu_j |U_ij|^2. Thus the candidate is equivalent, for this special cq ensemble, to

    H(Z|A)+H(Z|B) >= H(Z|AB)+H(Z|IJ).

This is NOT ordinary SSA, and the measurement I,J cannot be replaced by an arbitrary measurement. This reformulation is a precise gap rather than a proof.

## Proven: commuting states

For commuting r,s, N=J (the NS functional reduces to the classical JS functional even with eigenvalue degeneracies). The canonical pure-state Holevo bound J<=H(c) proves the candidate.

## Proven: equal-rank normalized projections, including all pure pairs

Suppose r=P/k and s=Q/k with P,Q projections of the same rank k. Let t_l in [0,1], l=1,...,k, be the squared cosines of their principal angles. The principal-angle decomposition gives

    c=(1/k) sum_l t_l,
    J=(1/k) sum_l H(sqrt(t_l)),
    N=1-c.

Since f(t)=H(sqrt(t)) is concave, J<=H(sqrt(c)). It is therefore enough to establish

    2H(sqrt(c))-H(c)-1+c <=0,  0<=c<=1.

Here is an exact scalar proof. Define g(c) as the left side. It is continuous, with g(0)=g(1)=0. For 0<c<1, its second derivative obeys the convergent expansion

    (ln 2) g''(c)
      = sum_{k>=0} (2k+2) c^(2k) [1/(4k+3)-c/(4k+5)] >=0.

Thus g is convex and lies below the chord between its zero endpoints. This proves the whole equal-rank projection class, with no numerical assumption.

For the concavity claim, the elementary entropy series is

    f(t)=1-(1/ln 2) sum_{n>=1} t^n/[2n(2n-1)],

whose second derivative is nonpositive on (0,1).

## Invalid shortcut explicitly excluded

The tempting universal estimate J<=H(sqrt(c)) is false. Take commuting r=|0><0| and s=I_d/d. Then c=d^(-1/2), while

    J=1 - [(d+1) log_2(d+1)-d log_2 d]/(2d).

Hence 1-J is asymptotic to (log_2 d)/(2d), whereas 1-H(sqrt(c)) is asymptotic to 1/(2 ln(2) sqrt(d)); for sufficiently large d, J>H(sqrt(c)). Therefore the projection-class proof does not extend
